newsitem.title: USA: Missouri to sue tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: Missouri to sue tobacco companies.

text.p: The state of Missouri said on Wednesday that it will sue the tobacco industry for targeting children in advertising and for lying to consumers about the addictive nature of nicotine.

Atty. Gen. Jeremiah Nixon said he was taking the action -- which will allege violation of state consumer protection laws -- in part to get the state into court before any industrywide settlement that might preclude future suits.
"We now have proof that the companies have broken the laws of Missouri by wilfully targeting young people and knowingly lying about the addictive nature of nicotine," he said.
Missouri was not among the 22 states which have sued tobacco companies to recover Medicaid money spent on health care for smokers.

Those states and other parties have been involved in secret negotiations which could lead to an across-the-board settlement worth $300 billion, according to some reports, and impose certain restrictions on the industry.

In March the smallest of the major cigarette makers, Liggett Group, owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd., reached a settlement with the attorneys general, becoming the first tobacco company to admit that nicotine is addictive and agreeing to turn over internal documents that could prove damaging to the entire industry.
Missouri's Nixon said that settlement "dramatically changes the posture of the litigation."

He added that Congressioal action as part of any industry-wide settlement could preclude future lawsuits so "It is important for Missouri to be on file in order to receive our fair share of any future settlements."
The announcement said the "major tobacco companies" would be named in the suit, but did specify them by name. It also did not specify what sort of redress or damage would be sought.

Philip Morris Cos. Inc., is the biggest U.S. tobacco company, followed by R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. and Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., a unit of Britain's B.A.T Industries.

Earlier on Wednesday, Pennsylvania filed suit against the major tobacco companies seeking to recover over $1 billion in Medicaid bills the state has paid to treat people from tobacco-related illnesses.
